record.title: Commission Implementing Decision of 23.6.2025 on a standardisation request to the European Committee for Standardisation and the European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardisation as regards high-risk AI-systems in support of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council and repealing Implementing Decision C(2023)3215
record.summary: A Commission implementing decision requesting CEN and Cenelec to draft harmonised standards and European standardisation deliverables supporting the AI Act's requirements for high-risk AI systems in Articles 9 to 15, 17 and 43. The standards cover ten areas: risk management, governance and quality of datasets, record keeping, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity, quality management and conformity assessment. High-risk AI systems that conform to harmonised standards referenced in the Official Journal are presumed to meet the requirements those standards cover. The standards must conform with Union law on fundamental rights and data protection.
record.notes: It repeals and replaces Implementing Decision C(2023) 3215 of 22 May 2023, which was based on the Commission's proposal for the AI Act: the new request reflects the final text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and sets a new deadline because CEN and Cenelec reported significant delays in September 2024, while the scope and technical content of the requested standards stay as in the 2023 request. CEN and Cenelec were to draft the standards and deliver their final report by 31 August 2025, update their work programme and report to the Commission every three months. The decision is addressed to CEN and Cenelec, ceases to apply if they do not accept the request, and expires on 28 February 2027. Applying the resulting standards remains voluntary. CEN and Cenelec work on them in Joint Technical Committee JTC 21; prEN 18286, a quality management system standard for AI Act purposes supporting Article 17, became the first harmonised standard for AI to enter public enquiry, on 30 October 2025. Under the request CEN and Cenelec completed the harmonised standard on quality management systems for providers of AI systems, including post-market monitoring (point 9 of Annex I), as EN 18286:2026; Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 of 12 October 2026 published its reference in the Official Journal on 14 October 2026, from when compliance with it gives a presumption of conformity.

verification.note: Re-read in the recheck of 17 Oct 2026: the Commission document-register PDF of C(2025) 3871 final (official, stored 11 Oct 2026; the decision's body without its annexes) confirms the title, the date 23.6.2025, the authentic languages, the repeal of C(2023) 3215, the 31 Aug 2025 deadline, three-monthly reporting and expiry on 28 Feb 2027. The Commission's AI Act standardisation page (stored 17 Oct 2026; its last update 3 Aug 2026) confirms the ten standardisation areas, JTC 21, the voluntary use of standards and prEN 18286 entering public enquiry on 30 Oct 2025. Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 of 12 Oct 2026 on EUR-Lex (stored 17 Oct 2026 with the browser retry) confirms that EN 18286:2026 was completed under this request and its reference published in OJ L of 14.10.2026. No amendment of the decision was found. The entry-into-force date (taken in version 1 as the adoption date) is not shown in the stored files; a decision addressed to its recipients takes effect on notification, whose date is not stored. Version 1's statements that EN 18286 was approved in June 2026 with its OJ citation pending, and that delays in standards justified the Digital Omnibus postponement, are not supported by the stored files and were removed.

judgment.status_reasoning: Adopted on 23.6.2025 and addressed to CEN and Cenelec (Article 6); Article 5 makes it expire on 28 February 2027, which is after today (17 Oct 2026). Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 of 12 Oct 2026 publishes EN 18286:2026, completed on the basis of this request, so the request was accepted and is being executed; the Commission's standardisation page (last update 3 Aug 2026) still describes it as current. No amendment or repeal was found. 'In force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A binding Commission implementing decision requesting the harmonised standards for the AI Act's high-risk requirements; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: The decision is dated 23.6.2025 on its cover page and in its closing formula.
